scale.usable_n_evidence: cohort article real_numbers: 'we retained a total of 4730 samples from 1519 participants. Of these, 1393 participants had plasma lipidome profiling since baseline… Most participants had visits at baseline (n = 1393), 12 months (n = 1188) and 24 months (n = 1089), with a decline in participant numbers in other time points' (PMC12269576)
scale.usable_n_for_request_reason: 1188 participants have both a baseline and at least one follow-up timepoint (12-month visit n=1188), satisfying longitudinal_required=true. For a biomarker validation design targeting the AD+MCI disease subset, the operative sub-groups are: AD discriminator set 580 subjects (243 stable AD + 337 stable CN) and MCI-to-AD converters 329. The 200-person minimum is exceeded under all sub-groupings.
scale.multi_site_potential: ADNI is a 60+ US site consortium under LONI governance; ASPREE (same Baker Institute platform, Agilent 6495C vs 6490) is the natural external validation partner — 724 of 781 lipid species overlap with documented NIST SRM 1950 cross-cohort harmonisation (PMC12269576), making pooled analysis feasible.
scale.axis_summary: Scale is a strong point: headline 1517, longitudinal-eligible 1188, minimum disease-subset 329 converters. All exceed the 200-person floor. The risk is not total N but analytical sub-group shrinkage in conversion prediction models.

source.evidence: pricing-data.md ADNI row: 'Data access: free via LONI portal (https://ida.loni.usc.edu). Requirements: DUA signature. Commercial use: allowed (public-private partnership).' Verified 2026-03-29. Confidence: PUBLISHED.
source.note: Base LONI DUA explicitly permits commercial use. ADMC lipidomics data sublayer may require a SEPARATE agreement with Duke University / Baker Institute — that agreement has no published cost and is flagged as a gap.

screening_qa.evidence: No QA re-processing cost appears in the wiki or pricing-data.md for ADNI-specific plasma lipidomics QA. Published QC procedures documented in cohort article sample_usability (PMC12269576): pooled plasma every 20 samples, blanks every 40 samples, NIST SRM 1950 every 40 samples.
screening_qa.note: If buyer accepts published QC-passed dataset (most likely for a validation study using existing data), QA leg is $0. If buyer commissions re-QA audit, analogous plasma metabolomics QA at academic core (Baylor/Duke tiers per pricing-data.md): $5–15/sample; at n=1188 that is $5,940–$17,820.

assay.estimate: already performed (Baker Institute Agilent 6490 dMRM, 781 lipid species, 4730 plasma samples)
assay.evidence: cohort article summary: '4730 plasma samples from 1517 participants profiled with Baker Heart and Diabetes Institute's targeted LC-MS/MS QqQ lipidomics platform (Agilent 6490, dMRM, 781 lipid species)' (PMC12269576). baker-institute-lipidomics-lc-ms-qqq platform article confirms assay completed for both ADNI and ASPREE.
assay.note: If buyer needs a fresh assay on new ADNI biospecimens via RARC/NIA, analogous targeted lipidomics at Duke core (high-res lipid profiling ESI+ and ESI-) is $517/sample non-Duke rate (pricing-data.md). At n=200 minimum that is ~$103,400 for a fresh targeted run.

unknowns: ADMC separate data agreement cost if required: no published figure; could range from $0 (waived for commercial partners) to $5K–$50K legal/DUA overhead (pricing-data.md gaps section)
Screening QA cost if buyer commissions re-QA audit beyond published QC
Physical biospecimen aliquot cost if buyer needs new wet samples (RARC/NIA route; no published per-sample ADNI figure in wiki)
cost.timeline: 2–4 months for standard LONI DUA data access; additional 4–12 weeks if ADMC commercial DUA negotiation is required; physical sample requests via RARC/NIA add further queue time (estimate +3–6 months based on NIA Aging Research Biobank operational norms in pricing-data.md)
cost.axis_summary: Source leg is $0 for data reuse under LONI DUA (commercial use allowed per pricing-data.md). Assay is a sunk cost for existing dataset. Two unknowns remain: whether the ADMC lipidomics sublayer requires a separate commercial agreement, and the cost of any buyer-side QA re-processing. Composite cost is open until ADMC commercial terms are confirmed.

pre_analytical.fasting: documented — ~95% fasting rate across diagnostic groups (94.8%–96.4%); cohort article demographic_composition (PMC12269576)
pre_analytical.tube_type: plasma confirmed (EDTA implied by ADNI standard protocol); extraction description in PMC12269576 mislabels samples as 'serum' — likely copy-paste error from prior methods paper (Alshehry et al., ref 46). Cohort article open_questions flags this explicitly.
pre_analytical.freeze_thaw: not documented in PMC12269576 or wiki; ADNI biospecimen protocol paper (Huynh et al. 2018, ref 20 in source) not yet ingested — flagged as gap in cohort article open_questions
pre_analytical.storage: not documented at this depth in wiki; NCRAD handles ADNI biospecimen storage but storage-specific pre-analytical parameters are not captured
pre_analytical.evidence: cohort article sample_usability: 'Quality control procedures included pooled plasma samples every 20 samples, blanks every 40 samples, and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Standard Reference Material (SRM) 1950 plasma every 40 samples' (PMC12269576)
pre_analytical.verdict: partial — fasting (load-bearing for lipidomics) is documented at 95%, and QC procedures are strong (NIST SRM 1950). Tube type is confirmed as plasma but EDTA is implied not stated. Freeze-thaw cycle count and storage duration are the two largest missing pre-analytical unknowns for metabolomics reproducibility.

statin_confounded.finding: 423 lipid species significantly associated with statin usage mapped and documented. Statin use controlled as a covariate in modelling. Evidence: cohort article medication_and_lifestyle_confounders: 'we identified 423 lipid species significantly associated with statin usage (Supplementary Table S6) and 398 lipid species associated with omega-3 usage (Supplementary Table S7), both after multiple testing correction' (PMC12269576).
statin_confounded.verdict: good — statin confounding is the request's primary hard_negative and it is explicitly addressed. Statin-associated species are mapped (n=423), documented in supplementary tables, and controlled as a covariate. A buyer can use this mapping to identify statin-sensitive species in their own target cohort.

commercial_use_allowed_false.finding: LONI DUA explicitly permits commercial use per pricing-data.md ('Commercial use: allowed (public-private partnership)'). However, the ADMC lipidomics data sublayer may require a separate agreement with Duke University / Baker Institute — that agreement's commercial terms are not stated in the wiki. cohort article open_questions flags: 'ADNI DUA terms for commercial use are not explicit in this paper. Buyers with commercial intent must verify with ADNI/ADMC whether the lipidomics data layer falls under the standard ADNI DUA or requires a separate ADMC agreement.'
commercial_use_allowed_false.verdict: partial — base LONI DUA permits commercial use per pricing-data.md, which is a positive signal. The ADMC lipidomics sublayer is the unresolved risk. This hard_negative is partially addressed but requires pre-commitment verification.

confounders.demographics: APOE e4 enriched by design (ADNI recruitment criterion); ~91% non-Hispanic White implied. Mean age >74. Cohort article demographic_composition: APOE e4 frequencies elevated in disease arm vs controls. Models may not generalise to diverse or younger-onset AD populations.
confounders.verdict: good on statin (the request's primary hard_negative). Commercial use is partially cleared — base DUA allows it but ADMC sublayer is unverified. Demographic homogeneity is a separate concern not flagged as a hard_negative.

platform_validation.platform: Baker Institute LC-MS/MS QqQ (Agilent 6490 dMRM, 781 lipid species, 49 lipid classes)
platform_validation.cohorts_using_this_platform: 2 entities in wiki (adni-go2-plasma-lipidomics and aspree-dementia-casecohort-lipidomics) both reference baker-institute-lipidomics-lc-ms-qqq as assay_platform
platform_validation.cross_cohort_validation: ADNI → ASPREE replication documented: C-index 0.75 (95% CI 0.73–0.78) in ASPREE (n=3495); HR=1.21 (p=9.85×10⁻⁴) for incident dementia (PMC12269576). NIST SRM 1950 harmonisation method documented in provenance_chain of ASPREE article.
platform_validation.verdict: good — platform is established for AD plasma lipidomics. Two independent cohorts (ADNI and ASPREE) have published results on this exact platform. Cross-cohort replication is documented.

quality.axis_summary: Quality is medium overall. The request's two hard_negatives are handled: statin confounding is explicitly addressed (423 species mapped, covariate-controlled), and commercial use is partially cleared (LONI DUA permits it; ADMC sublayer requires verification). Pre-analytical detail is the load-bearing weakness — freeze-thaw cycles and storage duration are undocumented. Provenance depth 0.48 (10 of 21 dimensions covered).

card_for_delivery.primary_signal: 1188 longitudinal-eligible plasma lipidomics participants (baseline + ≥1 follow-up) from ADNI-1/GO/2; disease sub-groups: 580 stable AD vs CN, 329 MCI-to-AD converters. Statin confounders explicitly mapped (423 species, covariate-controlled). Baker Institute Agilent 6490 dMRM, 781 species, NIST SRM 1950 QC.
card_for_delivery.action: Apply for LONI DUA access at ida.loni.usc.edu (commercial use permitted per published terms). Separately contact ADMC/Duke University team to confirm whether the lipidomics data sublayer requires an additional commercial agreement before committing project timeline.
card_for_delivery.risk: ADMC lipidomics sublayer commercial terms unverified — this is the single pre-commitment blocker. Freeze-thaw cycle count undocumented. The deDE lipid class (strongest AD signal in this paper) is excluded from usable modelling due to anticholinesterase confounding.

scale.usable_n_evidence: cohort article real_numbers: 'the case-cohort subset (n = 3495) contained incident dementia (n = 402) with an average follow-up of 6.5 years' (PMC12269576). Headline sub-cohort is 3495; full ASPREE trial is 19,114.
scale.usable_n_for_request_reason: The request requires Alzheimer's disease / dementia cases for biomarker validation. Within the 3495-person sub-cohort, only 402 are incident dementia cases with 6.5-year prospective follow-up. The 3093 cognitively normal comparators are available as controls. For a validation design testing a lipidomic model against true dementia outcomes, the operative case N is 402. This exceeds the 200-person minimum but only by a factor of 2, leaving limited headroom for sub-group analyses (e.g., by APOE genotype or sex). European-descent-only restriction further reduces generalisability.
scale.multi_site_potential: ASPREE is a single national trial (Australia, 64 general practices). Cross-cohort aggregation with ADNI is the most natural pairing — both use the Baker Institute platform (Agilent 6490/6495C, 724 of 781 species overlapping) with documented NIST SRM 1950 harmonisation (PMC12269576). However, ASPREE is population-based RCT while ADNI is clinic-recruited; pooling requires careful weighting.
scale.axis_summary: Scale is adequate but tight for the request. Headline sub-cohort is 3495 but the request-relevant case N is 402 incident dementia cases. Longitudinal follow-up (6.5 years) is a strength. Sub-group analyses are constrained at n=402.

source.estimate: quote required (PI-request-only access; no formal portal, no published pricing)
source.evidence: cohort article access_and_consent_scope: 'ASPREE data are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request.' (PMC12269576). No pricing figure exists in pricing-data.md for PI-request-only academic cohort access.
source.note: Academic access may be free or involve an MTA/DUA with nominal admin cost. Commercial use terms are unspecified — a commercial DUA could incur $5K–$50K in legal overhead (pricing-data.md gaps section: 'Legal/DUA overhead: highly variable $5K–$50K per agreement, institution-dependent').

screening_qa.evidence: No screening QA cost data in wiki for ASPREE. cohort article provenance_chain documents NIST SRM 1950 correction factors applied to harmonise ASPREE with ADNI (PMC12269576), but buyer-side re-QA cost is not captured.
screening_qa.note: If buyer plans joint ADNI+ASPREE analysis, cross-cohort QA harmonisation is documented. If buyer needs independent re-QA, costs analogous to ADNI estimate: $5–15/sample at academic core, or quote required for commercial QA lab.

assay.estimate: already performed (Baker Institute Agilent 6495C dMRM, 781 lipid species, n=3495 plasma samples)
assay.evidence: cohort article summary: 'Lipidomics was generated at Baker Heart and Diabetes Institute using the Agilent 6495C platform under identical chromatographic conditions as the ADNI Baker Institute platform, with 724 of 749 lipid species overlapping' (PMC12269576). baker-institute-lipidomics-lc-ms-qqq platform article references aspree-dementia-casecohort-lipidomics.
assay.note: Existing data reuse incurs no new assay cost. Fresh assay on ASPREE biospecimens (if any aliquots remain — status unknown) would be quote required from Baker Institute; no Baker Institute commercial assay pricing is in pricing-data.md.

cost.within_budget: unknown (request did not state budget; source leg is quote required)
unknowns: Source access cost: PI-request-only with no published pricing; academic access likely free but commercial DUA cost unknown
Commercial use terms: completely unspecified — ethics approval #523/21 (Alfred Hospital) does not address commercial use
Screening QA cost if buyer requires re-QA beyond original NIST SRM 1950 QC
Sample depletion status: aliquot inventory unknown, per cohort article open_questions
cost.timeline: 3–12 months (PI-request-only, no predictable timeline per cohort article access_and_consent_scope). Commercial negotiation would add further uncertainty. Physical sample availability is unknown — sample depletion risk is explicitly flagged.
cost.axis_summary: All three cost legs are either 'already performed' (assay) or 'quote required' (source, QA). The source cost is entirely unpredictable — PI-gated with no portal and no published pricing. Commercial use has no documented pathway, making the cost composite fully open.

pre_analytical.fasting: not documented in wiki for ASPREE — cohort article does not contain a fasting rate for ASPREE participants (only ADNI fasting rate ~95% is reported in PMC12269576)
pre_analytical.tube_type: plasma confirmed (ASPREE used same Baker Institute protocol as ADNI, Agilent 6495C dMRM); tube type implied plasma/EDTA but not explicitly stated in wiki
pre_analytical.freeze_thaw: not documented — cohort article open_questions explicitly flags: 'Freeze-thaw cycle count and time-from-venipuncture-to-freeze are not stated'
pre_analytical.evidence: cohort article provenance_chain: 'The ASPREE study (n = 3495) used as the validation study was run under identical chromatographic conditions, but using an Agilent 6495C. Both studies were conducted in batches of 486 samples… NIST SRM 1950 reference concentration…' (PMC12269576)
pre_analytical.verdict: weak — only instrument model and QC method (NIST SRM 1950) are documented. Fasting status, freeze-thaw cycles, storage duration, and tube type are missing from the wiki. For a metabolomics validation study, this is insufficient pre-analytical documentation.

statin_confounded.finding: Statin use in ASPREE is NOT documented in the wiki entity. The cohort article has no medication_and_lifestyle_confounders dimension (frontmatter covered_dimensions: only real_numbers, access_and_consent_scope, provenance_chain). ASPREE is an elderly Australian population (≥70 years) in which statin prevalence is likely high, but this is not evidenced in the wiki and cannot be scored.
statin_confounded.verdict: missing — statin confounding is the request's primary hard_negative, and ASPREE has no documentation of statin prevalence, statin-associated lipid species, or statin covariate adjustment in the wiki. This is a material gap for this request.

commercial_use_allowed_false.finding: Commercial use terms for ASPREE are completely unspecified. cohort article access_and_consent_scope: 'ASPREE data are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request.' Ethics approval #523/21 (Alfred Hospital Ethics Committee) is for academic research and does not address commercial use. No commercial use pathway is documented in any linked institution article.
commercial_use_allowed_false.verdict: missing — the request's hard_negative 'commercial_use_allowed_false' is directly applicable here. There is no documented commercial use pathway for ASPREE lipidomics data. This is a pre-commitment blocker.

confounders.demographics: European-descent-only restriction documented (cohort article real_numbers: 'refined the sub-cohort to include participants aged 70 years or older of European descent'). APOE e4/e4 homozygotes and e2/e2 homozygotes enriched in case-cohort per open_questions. Full demographic composition not covered in wiki.
confounders.verdict: weak — both hard_negatives (statin_confounded, commercial_use_allowed_false) are unaddressed in the wiki. Statin documentation is absent; commercial use pathway does not exist. This entity fails both hard_negative checks for this request.

platform_validation.platform: Baker Institute LC-MS/MS QqQ (Agilent 6495C dMRM, 781 lipid species, same platform family as ADNI)
platform_validation.cohorts_using_this_platform: 2 entities in wiki — adni-go2-plasma-lipidomics and aspree-dementia-casecohort-lipidomics both reference baker-institute-lipidomics-lc-ms-qqq
platform_validation.cross_cohort_validation: ASPREE is itself the validation cohort for ADNI-derived models. The lipidome risk score trained in ADNI achieved C-index 0.75 in ASPREE (PMC12269576). ASPREE's role is as the validation dataset, not an independent discovery cohort.
platform_validation.verdict: good for the platform itself (documented cross-cohort replication with ADNI). However, ASPREE as an independent starting point for new model development has only one published analysis (as validation target).

quality.axis_summary: Quality is low. Provenance depth is 0.14 — only 3 of 21 dimensions are covered. Both of the request's hard_negatives fail: statin confounding is undocumented, and commercial use has no pathway. Pre-analytical detail is weak (fasting unknown, freeze-thaw unknown). This entity cannot be responsibly scored above low quality confidence with current wiki coverage.

card_for_delivery.primary_signal: 402 incident dementia cases with 6.5-year prospective follow-up in a population-based Australian RCT (ASPREE); plasma lipidomics on Baker Institute Agilent 6495C (781 species, same platform as ADNI, NIST-harmonised). Request-relevant case N = 402 — exceeds 200-person floor but leaves limited sub-group headroom.
card_for_delivery.action: Contact Paul Lacaze (Monash University) and Peter Meikle (Baker Institute) to confirm: (1) whether commercial use is permitted under ASPREE ethics #523/21, and (2) whether lipidomics data and/or biospecimens are available. Do not commit project timeline until commercial use is confirmed.
card_for_delivery.risk: Both hard_negatives for this request are unresolved: statin confounding is entirely undocumented in the wiki, and no commercial use pathway exists. PI-gated access with 3–12 month unpredictable timeline. Sample depletion status unknown.
